newsitem.title: JAPAN: Kawasaki Steel says to limit capital investment.
newsitem.headline: Kawasaki Steel says to limit capital investment.

text.p: Kawasaki Steel Corp said on Tuesday it plans to limit parent company capital investment to about 40 billion yen annually in the two or three years beginning next fiscal year from April 1998.

"We plan to continue capital spending mainly for repairing and overhauling existing facilities in the future, because we already completed restructuring at the Chiba and Mizushima works," said Fumio Sudo, a director of the company.
The company said earlier on Tuesday that it plans parent capital investment of 45 billion yen in fiscal 1997/98.

Capital investment in 1997/98 includes part of the cost for overhauling the 20-year-old No 6 furnace at the Chiba works, Sudo said. Extending the life of the furnace will raise Kawasaki's competitiveness, he said.
The planned 1997/98 investment is the second-lowest of the past 20 years.
One of the major investments in 1997/98 will be a 9.2 billion yen project to increase capacity at its chip processing operations and to build chip development facilities, he said.
